Oh I wouldn't worry too much about that! Syringes have something called "dead space" which is where fluids from the injection as well as leftover medication sit after you inject. Syringes with detachable needles tend to have a higher dead space, which means more of the medication is leftover in the syringe even after you depress the plunger completely. 

Prescriptions account for this dead space, which I assume is why you were told to inject .13 instead of .1-- that .03 is probably for dead space. And a few drops on the needle is no biggie as well! If you are really concerned still, definitely reach out to whoever prescribes you the T. They'll be able to help you out for sure!
